title: Build an animated chart
summary: Build an animated bar chart in three stages: drawing the data, sequencing changes and accepting new values.
outcome: A bar chart that animates its data and responds to changes.

blocks.text: Build a release-time chart that first shows fixed data, then reveals its bars, and finally lets the reader compare a second dataset by clicking. Each stage below is a complete scene you can edit and run.

We will compare the time spent building, testing and shipping a release. The category stays attached to its value, so a changing bar is easy to follow. Start by editing one value and checking the labels before adding animation.
`BarChart` comes from `retiam/charts`; `Scene` and the camera come from `retiam`. The chart uses a fixed `yRange` of zero to 100 minutes. This preserves a stable scale when comparing datasets.
The second version adds one awaited `BarChart.animateIn` call. The chart already knows its final geometry; the animation introduces that geometry over 1200 milliseconds.
Keep the entrance brief enough that the audience can read the values. A decorative reveal should support the comparison. Change duration to 400 and then 2400 milliseconds to judge the tradeoff.
Click any bar after the entrance to alternate datasets. `InteractionManager` dispatches the bar’s click; a busy flag prevents conflicting updates if the reader clicks repeatedly.

`BarChart.animateData` updates existing bars by index using the established scale. Keep category count and order fixed here. It does not rebuild categories or recompute the axis domain; rebuild a chart deliberately if those must change.
Use it in your own application
Use units in the title or value suffix and keep comparisons on the same scale. Validate finite values before creating the chart.
Animate updates from user actions or actual data changes. Keep the data model outside the scene when integrating with an application, and destroy the scene when its canvas is removed.
Next, compare other chart types in [Charts](/charts) or inspect the [chart gallery](/examples-charts).
